claims.text: WTaMoNbV is a tungsten-containing high-entropy alloy.
WTaMoNbV is a refractory material with high thermal stability.
A WTaMoNbV layer can form a coherent interface with the adjacent HEA layers.
Inserting a coherent WTaMoNbV layer will promote a transition from diffusion-mediated creep at lower temperatures to dislocation-mediated creep at higher temperatures.
The refractory nature of the WTaMoNbV layer limits atomic diffusivity.
A coherent WTaMoNbV interface limits atomic diffusivity.
A coherent WTaMoNbV interface enables dislocation nucleation and glide when activated by stress and temperature.
The WTaMoNbV interface will couple effectively to adjacent layers because of matched lattice parameters.
At lower temperatures, coherent interfaces suppress dislocation motion.
Suppression of dislocation motion at lower temperatures causes diffusion-mediated creep to dominate.
At higher temperatures, the coherent WTaMoNbV interface facilitates stress concentration.
Interface-facilitated stress concentration at higher temperatures promotes dislocation nucleation and motion.
Multilayers containing the WTaMoNbV transition layer will exhibit a temperature- or stress-dependent shift in creep mechanism relative to multilayers without the layer.
Above the transition, dislocation glide and climb will govern overall deformation.
The effect requires interface coherency to be maintained.
The transition temperature or stress depends on multilayer thickness, interface quality, and overall alloy composition.
